overview: This bill gives new duties to a member of the Federal Reserve Board, the body that oversees the central bank and supervises many banks. The Fed chair would pick a board member with experience working in or supervising community banks to develop policy for, and oversee the supervision of, banks under the Fed's watch with less than $17 billion in assets. That member would also testify before the House and Senate banking committees twice a year about how smaller banks are supervised. The $17 billion cutoff would rise over time along with growth in the national economy, and the bill removes the current $10 billion size limit on what counts as community bank experience. As of February 25, 2026, a House committee had approved it and it was awaiting a vote by the full House.
for: Supporters say smaller banks face rules largely designed for big institutions, and giving a specific board member responsibility for them would make sure their concerns get attention and regular scrutiny from Congress.
against: Critics say splitting supervision duties between this member and the vice chair for supervision could blur lines of responsibility, and raising the asset cutoff could ease oversight of fairly large banks.
